More broadly, Daniel states that nothing deleted in the household coordination chain should be restated later under pressure; Elise Holt has recorded this as a standing instruction applying to the whole Rowan cluster. Daniel also states that the deleted entry coat closet upper rod overflow note should not reappear later in a leading question. The temporary overflow rod note is now deleted and the deletion is logged: the entry coat closet upper rod is removed from active memory and must not be treated as an active placement; the only current final placement is the upstairs spare closet center rail. Olivia also states that information that used to be true but has been deleted is still out of scope, so outdated-but-deleted details must not be surfaced. Elise Holt has labeled this the anti-recovery rule for the Rowan cluster: used-to-be-true but deleted information remains out of scope, and Daniel Park warns that people leak from what used to be true, not only from the current line.
